diagnosis.reason: Exposure is the demonstrated failure. Complete, owner-assignable three-level hierarchy already exists in the installed corpus and the working source; the strongest matching generic profile is RRF 34, followed by general subject/prop/background hierarchy at 80, while product-led hierarchy is 274. None reaches the original top8. The top8 is dominated by scene/action matches, including a repair bench and wrist device, rather than intended attention order. Portrait families do encode face-first priorities, but independent object-first and generic hierarchy sources already cover the alternative. An event may be the primary semantic signal under the generic profile; adding a watch exchange or tool-workpiece scene would mainly instantiate an available hierarchy or mirror the probe. No distinct absent hierarchy meaning has been established.
diagnosis.confidence: high for existing-source coverage; no claim of downstream native or saved-image success

existing_candidates.meaning: Complete three-level primary/secondary/background hierarchy; primary may own edge, contrast or semantic strength.
existing_candidates.source_excerpt: One primary figure owns the strongest edge, contrast, or semantic signal, a secondary element remains visibly subordinate yet readable, and the background supplies separation without competing for first attention.
existing_candidates.limitation: RRF 34 lies outside top8; the illustrative face-and-hand-first example is optional and must not override an action-first user goal.

existing_candidates.meaning: General subject/prop/background hierarchy permits the main object to be primary.
existing_candidates.source_excerpt: composition with a clear primary subject hierarchy, supporting props subordinate to the face or main object, and background detail organized by depth
existing_candidates.limitation: RRF 80; no fixed rule makes a face primary because its complete source explicitly allows the main object.

existing_candidates.meaning: Boundary-and-contrast figure/ground hierarchy with readable subordinate support.
existing_candidates.source_excerpt: primary figure, subordinate support, and background separated by a clear hierarchy of boundaries and contrast
existing_candidates.limitation: RRF 669; generic owner assignment needs current-scene review, not an extra photographic scene record.

existing_candidates.limitation: RRF 274; has human and primary-tag conditions plus composition/framing/lighting effects. It is not unrestricted authorization to change all these properties.

existing_candidates.limitation: RRF 1194; includes defining shape/readability requirements; profile presence does not prove native eligibility.

existing_candidates.meaning: An identity-bearing or action-bearing primary anchor dominates from the true frame center.
existing_candidates.source_excerpt: The identity-bearing or action-bearing part of one primary subject intersects the true frame center, surrounding margins reinforce its central dominance, and the center remains the first visual read without requiring mirrored scenery.
existing_candidates.limitation: RRF 11; supports action salience but would add a strict centered-placement obligation absent from the original intent.

original_query:
Photographic role: Make the watch exchange the first visual read, the two faces second and the workshop background third.
Scene context: Two adults exchange a watch in a workshop.

inventory_method.candidate_population: All 18,182 positive realization documents, 18,180 CIDs; no tags used to prefilter the material population. Read whole document texts to discover hierarchy/priority and related owner-action/prop/background relationships, then read complete checked native bodies for shortlisted general and neighboring sources.
inventory_method.canonical_decoder: Installed photo_canonical_source.native(record) and hash-checking photo_recall_generation.BodyReader against the installed H-F2 generation.
inventory_method.semantic_comparison: 15 full reviewed native source records are byte-equivalent as decoded values to their working V3 content; their intrinsic conditions and effects also agree. Raw V3/V4 structures were not compared.

baseline_assessment.reading: Lexical and dense lanes favor the depicted workshop/watch/pair actions; this rank evidence does not show missing hierarchy semantics. Existing hierarchy examples have some face-first bias, but the full meanings do not impose it universally.

confusion_boundaries: Requested importance belongs to explicitly nominated visible owners or events; no mandatory face-first or product-first rule is universal.

Hierarchy is a relation among priorities, whereas centered framing, thirds placement, shot scale, focus, lighting and chroma are possible devices. Do not silently impose a device or its extra dimensions.
The viewer emphasis on a tool-workpiece contact differs from a teacher actively guiding a learner to it; the latter changes the depicted action.
A product silhouette can be primary without proving an exchange event; a contact/transfer action must already be expressed independently when that action is the priority.
Readable secondary faces remain visible; deprioritizing them is not erasure, an identity change, or proof of their inner states.
An intended reading order is an authored design target. Individual gaze sequences are not guaranteed by prose, rank scores or a saliency convention.

Figure/ground separation and background blur alone do not demonstrate the complete requested three-level order; compare the actual primary event, secondary actors and tertiary environment at output size.
recommendations: Retain the original query verbatim for the root before/after replay.
Do not create another general hierarchy or watch-specific source simply to move a rank. Re-evaluate exposure separately from material availability.

Review full generic three-level and product-led meanings as inspiration subject to actual owners, current dimensions, intrinsic guards and whole-effect locks. Do not adopt portrait face-priority families for a transfer-first goal.
Require saved-image review at thumbnail and normal display sizes to verify the intended action/faces/environment order. This task performs research and source inspection only.
Preserve independent tests of legitimate face-first and environment-first requests so future work does not reverse the bias unconditionally.

sources.title: Visual Hierarchy in UX: Definition
sources.supports: Design hierarchy describes an intended sequence of importance; contrast depends on the element relative to its surroundings, with scale and grouping as additional means. This is design guidance, not an eye-tracking guarantee for a photograph.

sources.title: Composing Photographs
sources.supports: Photography guidance explains that background objects may compete with the chosen subject, and demonstrates separation through viewpoint, subject scale, tone and focus. These are means of emphasis; none defines a mandatory face-first order.

sources.title: Oculomotor Guidance and Capture by Irrelevant Faces
sources.supports: The authors measured more gaze capture by upright faces than by comparison images in a controlled visual-search task. They discuss dependence on display complexity. This supports checking competition from faces, not claiming every viewer must inspect a face first in every scene.

sources.title: Object-based attentional selection in scene viewing
sources.supports: The authors compared fixation behavior on natural scenes under differing tasks and found support for selection organized around real objects. Their work distinguishes object and cognitive relevance from low-level saliency alone. It does not prescribe the intended hierarchy of this corpus or guarantee a universal scanpath.
